Replay

Visual cues

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Cues(Value) consumes journal changes into a bounded set of visible instances. Use copied presentation values: positions, colors, labels with fixed storage, or asset handles. Reference-bearing payloads are rejected at initialization. A cue does not retain a simulation entity or Godot node.

Odin
cues: view.Cues(Impact)
view.cues_init(&cues, epoch, baseline)
defer view.cues_destroy(&cues)

view.cues_advance(&cues, frame_seconds)
for change in changes {view.cues_change(&cues, change, 0.8)}
for cue in cues.slots {
    if !cue.active {continue}
    // Present cue.value with cue.key as the renderer's instance identity.
}

Begin creates an instance. Update changes its value in place; Confirm marks it confirmed. Neither restarts its lifetime. Cancel hides it immediately. Repeated Begin, including after cancellation or expiry, cannot replay a consumed ID. The renderer reconciles active keys each frame, so canceled/expired instances are removed and a recycled slot cannot inherit the previous node's identity. cues_change returns true only for a new instance.

The default pool holds 128 instances. Allocation happens at initialization; frame updates allocate nothing. A full pool drops the new visual and retains its consumed ID, so later retries cannot unexpectedly play it. stats exposes drops, duplicates, begins, updates, confirmations and cancellations. Serial exhaustion also drops new visuals explicitly. These are cosmetic limits, not simulation failure modes.

cues_clear stops active instances while retaining consumed IDs. cues_epoch accepts only a strictly newer epoch and resets the ledger to an explicit baseline. Call one_shots_retire(&cues.ledger, through) with a monotonic frontier behind which no new Begin can arrive; retain enough history for the runner's correction/watch window. Queued confirmed changes may predate a same-epoch checkpoint rebase: consume them before advancing the frontier past their ticks. Recreating an effect owner is appropriate when leaving a session, not for an ordinary correction.

This helper tracks visual lifetimes, not deterministic particle trajectories or irreversible sound/external effects. The journal still determines prediction and confirmation policy. A renderer may move, recolor or remove an active effect, but already displayed frames cannot be undone.
